turns.t: Morning, doctor! I'm Donna, I'm Leo's foster carer, we've had him eight months. He's two and a half, and I'm worried because he's not talking.
Hello Donna, hello Leo. Leo, what have you got there? ~
Car. ~
A car! Does it go fast? ~
Brum. ~
That's about it, doctor. He says car, brum, no, and mama, which he says to everyone. Not much else.
Does he put two words together, like 'more juice' or 'big car'?
Never. He points, and grunts, and gets frustrated and throws things.
Does he follow instructions, like 'give me the ball' or 'where's your shoe'?
Sometimes. If you show him. If you just say it, he doesn't always seem to understand.
Has he had a hearing test, or lots of ear infections?
He had loads of ear infections before he came to me, and grommets put in at eighteen months.
Any other medical history, or anything about his birth I should know?
He was born early, at thirty-two weeks. That's in his notes.
Is he on any medicines?
Vitamin D drops, once a day. I give them every morning.
Mama. ~
Hmm, I'm not sure I give them every day, if I'm honest. When it's chaos in the morning, I forget.
That's very normal. I'll note that they're meant to be daily and that some days are missed. Does he go to nursery, or have other children around?
Nursery three days a week, and his foster brother is five.
Does he make eye contact and play with others? ~
Yes, he loves cuddles, he waves bye-bye, he plays peekaboo. He's a very sociable boy. ~
That's reassuring, because those are good signs for social development. Let me examine him. Leo, can I look in your ears? ~
No. ~
Just a quick look, with a torch.
The grommets are in place, both ears look clean and dry, and I can see no fluid behind the eardrums.
Is it his hearing, then? ~
It might be partly. With his history of ear infections, hearing is the first thing to check. Overall, I think this is speech delay, probably related to the early ear problems and prematurity.
Will he catch up? ~
Many children do, especially with support. I'd like to arrange a hearing test, an audiology assessment, and a referral to the speech and language therapist.
How long will that take? ~
A few weeks for the hearing test. Meanwhile, talk to him constantly, name things, read picture books, and don't finish his sentences for him.
I do like a book. ~
And reduce screen time. If he loses words he already has, or seems not to respond to loud sounds, come back sooner.
I will. Thank you so much. ~
